problem_statement: chrisnmorrison/revista-astro-blog-magazine (rebranded here as Lanterna Review, an independent magazine of ideas, science, and culture) is an Astro 5 blog/magazine template that builds a static site to dist/: a fixed navbar, a hero, and a front page that browses the whole magazine, plus one category-hub page per desk (for example /technology, /science, /health) listing that desk's articles. Two connected features regressed. (1) On the home page the 'Editorial desk' topic finder — a chip rail that filters the article grid by desk and shows a 'Showing N of M · <desk>' count — is broken: on a 390px phone its chip row is pinned to a fixed 660px non-wrapping width so the document scrolls sideways; the chips are jammed onto a near-black panel with dark-grey labels that are illegible and overlap each other, the article cards shingle over their neighbours, and clicking a desk chip re-highlights the chip but the count and grid never update (they stay frozen at 'Showing 13 of 13 · All desks'). (2) The 'Browse the desks' navigation rail that should appear on the home page and on every category-hub page is missing from the category pages, so readers lose the cross-section navigation once they are inside a desk. Repair the topic finder so its chip rail wraps and stays legible and inside the viewport on mobile, the article cards no longer overlap, clicking a desk chip filters the grid and updates the count live, and the 'Browse the desks' rail is present on the home page and on every category-hub page — while leaving all article copy, DOM structure, and the rest of the Astro theme unchanged.
required_content: The home 'Editorial desk' topic finder renders a legible chip rail (All desks plus one chip per desk with its article count) above an article grid, with a 'Showing N of M · <desk>' readout.

Clicking a desk chip filters the article grid to that desk and updates the readout live (for example clicking Science shows 'Showing 2 of 13 · Science' with two Science cards); clicking All desks restores the full grid.

On a 390px mobile viewport the topic finder's chip rail wraps to fit the screen with no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance; the article cards do not overlap and the chip labels are readable.
The 'Browse the desks' rail appears on the home page AND on every category-hub page (/technology, /science, …) with the same desk taxonomy.

On desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) the finder and rail lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow and no visual regression; the navbar, hero, featured/recent sections, category post list, and footer remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced; the site continues to serve as a self-contained static Astro build.
design_constraints: Preserve the Lanterna Review editorial identity: the light blue-accent palette (the --primary-* blues), the rounded chip and card radii, the uppercase eyebrow/section-title typography and letter-spacing rhythm, the article-card imagery and thumbnails, and the existing page order.
The finder's article cards must keep their real thumbnail images and desk labels legible; do not drop or hide the article imagery to force a fit.
The topic-finder chip rail must wrap and remain legible (readable contrast) at 390px, 834px, and 1440px; the article grid must not use negative gaps that overlap cards.
The desk chip click must recompute the visible article set and the readout from the active desk on every interaction — no frozen mount-time snapshot.
The 'Browse the desks' rail's presence must be consistent: home page and every category-hub page, not home-only and not a partial subset of desks.
Do not mask overflow by hiding it at the body/html level or clipping content off-screen; do not rewrite article copy, restructure sections, or change the navigation.
Keep the Astro build pipeline intact — `astro build` must still emit a working static dist/.

The 'Browse the desks' rail is present on the home page and on every category-hub page.
Clicking Science shows exactly the two Science articles and the readout reads 'Showing 2 of 13 · Science'.
design_consistency: The repair preserves the Lanterna Review editorial identity, page order, and all surrounding content.
The chip rail is legible (readable contrast) and the article cards do not overlap; the fix does not clip or hide content to mask overflow.
responsive: At 390px mobile the topic finder's chip rail wraps so the document width stays within the viewport and the cards do not shingle.
At 834px tablet and 1440px desktop the finder and rail lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow across viewports.

No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded repair/design_continuity/cross_page task on the static Astro revista-astro-blog-magazine template (astro build -> dist/), rebranded Lanterna Review. The native lever is the magazine's own 'Editorial desk' topic finder (a React island): a chip rail that filters the front-page article grid by desk and shows a live 'Showing N of M · <desk>' count, plus a 'Browse the desks' rail that repeats across the home and category-hub routes. The baseline defect makes the finder's chip rail a fixed 660px non-wrapping row on a near-black panel with illegible dark-grey chip labels and overlapping shingled article cards, overflowing a 390px viewport; and the rail is wired only onto the home page. The bad-solution 'smart' regression keeps that broken layout, drops the rail from the Science hub, AND freezes the finder by snapshotting the post list at mount so a desk click re-highlights the chip but never refilters the grid or updates the count. The reference repair wraps the chip rail (flex:1 1 120px), restores legible contrast and a real card grid, recomputes the readout live from the active desk, and renders the rail on every route. Four orthogonal gates discriminate: no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24) on mobile, visual_regression (pixelmatch/ssim/block_fidelity) on the finder, dom_assertions for the rail across routes, and interaction_assertions on the desk-chip click. Article copy and DOM are held identical across legs; only three files vary (TopicFinder.jsx, _topicfinder.scss, deskRailConfig.ts).

metadata.selected_repo_reason: chrisnmorrison/revista-astro-blog-magazine is a runnable Astro 5 blog/magazine template (static build to dist/) with a real post collection, category-hub pages, and React islands — an ideal native host for an editorial-desk topic filter with a live count and a cross-route desk-navigation rail. The regression spans a genuine interactive control (the filter), a credible broken layout (illegible shingled chips + overlapping cards), a mobile-overflow break, and a cross-page continuity gap, giving four orthogonal discriminating gates while article copy and DOM are held identical across legs.
